extra.message: Admin Disabling a User Does Not Revoke Existing API Keys or Session Tokens

metadata.proof: When a marketplace_admin sets `is_active=False` on a user via `admin_users.py:update_user`, the route only toggles `User.is_active`. It does NOT: (1) revoke any of the user's API keys (ApiKey records remain with `is_active=True`), (2) invalidate existing JWT session tokens (they remain cryptographically valid and the server has no blocklist), or (3) expire pending password reset tokens. While `get_current_user` checks `user.is_active` at the DB level (so subsequent requests fail during suspension), the stale JWT tokens and API keys remain valid: if the user is later re-enabled, all previously issued tokens and keys become immediately usable again without any administrative action. Additionally, the JWT tokens have no `jti` claim or server-side revocation mechanism. SOURCE: admin sets `is_active=False`. SINK: no cascade to ApiKey.is_active or token blocklist.
